articles.title: Aspen: Self-hostable Git server for agent-scale traffic
articles.summary: A self-hostable Git server for agent-scale traffic: packs in object storage, per-branch history in Postgres. Pre-alpha. Aspen is a Git server you run yourself, built for repositories that hundreds of agents, CI jobs and people push to and fetch from at the same time. It speaks plain Git over HTTP and SSH, so stock git works with no client changes. It stores packs in object storage, keeps branch history in PostgreSQL, and runs on one machine or on any cloud. articles.title: The Docker group is root access, my agent used it to write to /etc.
articles.summary: I just learned that I have been running docker on my machine with passwordless sudo for the last uhm 10 years or so. I added my user to the docker group and with that anyone who takes over my user can just mount / and write as root everywhere ... But the most embarrassing thing is how I found out. I told a agent to do something and it realized it has to change a config in /etc/ but didn't have sudo, so it just mounted it with docker, bam! And I was so confused how it could write in /etc without sudo.

articles.title: Closed AI models dominate the price-performance frontier
articles.summary: At almost every budget, the best AI model you can buy is closed. An open-weight model wins at just 3% of price points, down from 41% in June. Village’s LLM Atlas maps the price-performance frontier: the strongest AI model at every price point. Open models win on value in bursts: a strong, cheap release, usually from DeepSeek, takes a wide band of budgets until the next closed model undercuts it.
